notes: Defect: promo code discount amount is not displayed correctly for return trip tickets in Mozio email confirmations. The return-trip mapping path (create-reservations.mappers.ts getTripData/RETURN_TRIP_TAIL) swaps from/to stations but likely does not propagate or correctly compute the discount amount for the return dispatch report. The sanitized dispatch mapper (map-to-sanitized-mozio-dispatch.ts) reads discount from dispatch.report.price.discount, so the root cause is upstream in how the discount is applied to the return-trip dispatch report before it reaches the mapper. apply-report-discounts.service.ts and map-line-item-return-trip-modification.ts are also in the data flow that feeds the dispatch report for return trips.

notes: Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria but excellent root-cause analysis identifying the data flow through create-reservations.mappers.ts (RETURN_TRIP_TAIL station swap), apply-report-discounts.service.ts, map-to-sanitized-mozio-dispatch.ts, and map-line-item-return-trip-modification.ts. I built ACs from scratch based on that analysis. AC1 is the core defect verification. AC2 ensures no regression on one-way trips. AC3 covers the no-discount edge case. AC4 covers percentage-based promo codes (a common variant). AC5 targets the dispatch report layer specifically, since the mapper reads from dispatch.report.price.discount and the root cause is upstream. AC6 addresses error handling for missing/malformed discount data. AC7 directly targets the suspected root cause — the station-swap in RETURN_TRIP_TAIL losing or corrupting the discount. AC8 covers the line-item modification path also identified in the data flow.
